question.text: In hydrogen discharge tube, it is observed that through a given cross-section <math><mn>3.13</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></math> electrons are moving from right to left and <math><mn>3.12</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></math> protons are moving from left to right per second. The current in the discharge tube (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mA</mi></math>) will be

solution.text:
Number of electrons ne=3.13×1015

Number of protons np=3.12×1015

Now, the current is given by the relation

i=neqe+npqp

=3.13×1015×1.6×10-19+3.12×1015×1.6×10-19

=1×10-3=1 mA

Now, due to excess the charge on electrons, the direction of the current will be towards the right.
